# Playwright TypeScript Examples

A collection of [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/) test examples written in TypeScript, covering UI automation, API testing, network mocking/interception, visual regression, waits, and test configuration.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 20+
- npm

## Setup

```bash
npm install
npx playwright install chromium
```

## Running tests

```bash
# Run the full suite (HTML report is generated by default)
npx playwright test

# Run a single file
npx playwright test tests/api.spec.ts

# Run in headed mode / UI mode
npx playwright test --headed
npx playwright test --ui

# Open the last HTML report
npx playwright show-report

# View a recorded trace
npx playwright show-trace test-results/<test-folder>/trace.zip
```

## Project structure

```
.
├── playwright.config.ts        # Global config (Chromium project, HTML reporter, traces on)
├── tests/
│   ├── api.spec.ts                     # REST API testing with the `request` fixture (GET/POST)
│   ├── demo-todo-app.spec.ts           # Playwright's sample TodoMVC tests (24 tests)
│   ├── example.spec.ts                 # Basic page navigation and assertions
│   ├── locators.spec.ts                # Locator strategies (role, placeholder, text, label, alt text, title)
│   ├── mock-api.spec.ts                # Mocking API responses with page.route / route.fulfill
│   ├── monitor-intercept-api.spec.ts   # Monitoring requests, aborting and modifying requests
│   ├── switchtab.spec.ts               # Handling new tabs/popups and switching between them
│   ├── test-config.spec.ts             # File-level config overrides via test.use
│   ├── traceviewer.spec.ts             # Generating traces for the Trace Viewer
│   ├── visualtest.spec.ts              # Visual regression with toHaveScreenshot (+ masking, diff ratios)
│   ├── visualtest.spec.ts-snapshots/   # Baseline screenshots (generated locally, gitignored)
│   └── wait.spec.ts                    # Waiting strategies (waitForResponse, waitForSelector, waitForFunction)
```

## Configuration highlights

From `playwright.config.ts`:

- **testDir:** `./tests` — Playwright only discovers specs inside this folder. A file path passed on the command line is a filter on discovered files, so specs outside `tests/` report "No tests found".
- **Browser:** Chromium only (Firefox/WebKit/mobile projects are commented out)
- **Reporter:** `html`
- **Trace:** always on
- **Video:** off locally, `retain-on-failure` on CI
- **Retries / workers:** 2 retries and 1 worker when `CI` is set
- **Emulation:** geolocation (Rome) and `Europe/Rome` timezone

Config precedence: file level (`test.use`) > project level > global level.

## Visual tests

Baseline screenshots live in `tests/visualtest.spec.ts-snapshots/`, which is **gitignored** (`*-snapshots/` in `.gitignore`). They are not shared through the repo, so each machine and CI environment creates its own:

- **First run:** when a baseline is missing, Playwright saves the current screenshot as the new baseline and reports the test as failed. Run the visual tests once more and they will compare against it.
- **Platform-specific:** baselines are named per browser and OS (e.g. `*-chromium-darwin.png`, `*-chromium-linux.png`), so a baseline made on macOS is never used on Linux CI.

To regenerate baselines after an intended UI change:

```bash
npx playwright test tests/visualtest.spec.ts --update-snapshots
```

The flipkart.com tests screenshot only the visible viewport (not the full page) and mask the rotating banners/images, with `maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.02`, because the homepage content changes on every load.
